title: MSFS massive franchise sale: 30% off MSFS 2024 & 30 unbundled aviator aircraft!
description:
Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 has officially launched its steepest anniversary franchise sale across Steam, the Xbox Store, and the Windows Store. Whether you are upgrading your base simulator or expanding your virtual hangar, this Microsoft Flight Simulator sale brings major price cuts across all MSFS 2024 editions, deep legacy discounts for MSFS 2020 and FSX Steam Edition, and the unbundling of 30 previously locked Aviator Edition aircraft into standalone packs.

In this MSFS buyer's guide and news breakdown, we explore all simulator discounts, how the new Famous Flyers and Local Legends aircraft packs work, how to claim the free 86-minute official MSFS orchestral soundtrack on Steam before September 1st, and step-by-step flight tutorials for the Antonov An-225, Junkers Ju 52, and ATR 42-600 / ATR 72-600.

⏱️ Video Chapters & Timestamps:

1:16 - Antonov An-225: 6-Engine Startup & Fuel Logic Tutorial
1:26 - Junkers Ju 52: VOR & Classic Radio Navigation Guide
1:39 - ATR 42-600 / 72-600: VNAV Descent & APP Mode Landing Guide
1:55 - Which MSFS pack are you buying?

✈️ MSFS Sale Discounts & Edition Comparison:

- Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024: 30% off across Standard, Deluxe, Premium Deluxe, and Aviator Edition.
- Microsoft Flight Simulator 2020: 65% off on Steam and Windows Store.
- FSX (Flight Simulator X: Steam Edition): 80% off historical low price.
- Free Steam Reward: Claim the 86-minute official MSFS orchestral soundtrack for free until September 1st.

📦 New Aviator Aircraft Packs (10 Aircraft per Pack for $39.99):
Instead of purchasing the full Aviator Edition upgrade, owners of MSFS Standard, Deluxe, or Premium Deluxe can now cherry-pick specific aircraft:

- Famous Flyers Pack 1: Includes heavy vintage and modern highlights such as the six-engine Antonov An-225.
- Local Legends Pack 1: Classic vintage aviation favorites, including the Junkers Ju 52.
- Local Legends Pack 2: Regional airliners and vintage turboprops including the ATR 42-600 and ATR 72-600.
